title: Cron and automation
summary: Robots should do the boring jobs at 3 a.m. Read and write crontabs, learn why a script that works by hand fails under cron, dodge the % trap, and retire Gary's most dangerous job.

nodes.oreo: the automation server, running a cron daemon

tasks.title: Read Gary's crontab
tasks.text: Gary left a job in root's crontab. Have a look (`crontab -l`). At what **hour** of the day does `cleanup-crumbs` run? (24-hour clock, just the hour.)
hints: A crontab line is five time fields and then the command: `minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week command`.
`30 4 * * 1-5` means minute 30 of hour 4 (04:30), any day of the month, any month, Monday to Friday.

tasks.title: Every five minutes
tasks.text: Brenda wants the oven report written all day long. Add a job to root's crontab that runs `/usr/local/bin/bake-report` **every 5 minutes**. Keep Gary's job for now.

checks.fail_msg: No crontab line runs bake-report every 5 minutes yet (crontab -l to check).
Gary's cleanup-crumbs line disappeared. Keep it for now (task 5 deals with it).

hints: On a real server, `crontab -e` opens the crontab in an editor and installs it on save. The in-page terminal cannot run an editor, so build the new crontab with a pipe instead (the last hint shows how): `crontab` still checks the syntax before it installs anything.
`*/5` in the minute field means "every 5th minute". So: `*/5 * * * * /usr/local/bin/bake-report`.
Without an editor: `(crontab -l; echo '*/5 * * * * /usr/local/bin/bake-report') | crontab -` (list the old jobs, add one, install the lot).

tasks.title: It works on my machine
tasks.text: Run `sync-sprinkles` in your terminal: it works. Now schedule it to run **every minute** from root's crontab... and wait a minute. Then read cron's mail to root: `cat /var/mail/root`. Fix things so that the job really **succeeds under cron**. (`minicron --run-now sync-sprinkles` runs your job right away, exactly the way cron would.)

checks.fail_msg: No crontab line runs sync-sprinkles every minute (* * * * *) yet.
The job fails when cron runs it. Run: minicron --run-now sync-sprinkles, and look at the error.

hints: The mail says `sprinkle-tool: not found`. But it runs fine by hand! What is different? Compare `echo $PATH` in your shell with the PATH cron uses (see the lesson).
Find where the tool really lives: `type sprinkle-tool`. Your interactive shell found it because `~/.bashrc` adds `/opt/sprinkles/bin` to PATH. Cron doesn't read `.bashrc`.
Two good fixes: put `PATH=/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/opt/sprinkles/bin` on a line **above** the job in the crontab, or make the script call `/opt/sprinkles/bin/sprinkle-tool` by its full path.

solution.note: This is the number one cron surprise. Cron starts jobs with a tiny environment (PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, no .bashrc, no aliases, sh instead of bash). Use full paths or set PATH at the top of the crontab.

tasks.title: The percent trap
tasks.text:
Add a job that runs every night at **02:00** and makes a dated backup of the crumbs folder, with exactly this command:

```
tar -czf /root/backups/crumbs-$(date +%F).tgz -C /srv crumbs
```

It works perfectly when you type it in the shell. In a crontab, it does not, unless you know cron's little secret about one of those characters. Make it work (test with `minicron --run-now /root/backups`).

checks.fail_msg: No crontab line runs the backup at 02:00 (0 2 * * *) yet.
When cron runs the job, no /root/backups/crumbs-<today>.tgz appears. Try: minicron --run-now /root/backups

hints: Run it the cron way and read the error: `minicron --run-now /root/backups`. The command looks cut short...
In a crontab, `%` is special: cron turns the first `%` into the end of the command (the rest becomes the job's input). `man 5 crontab` on a real system says so in one easily missed sentence.
Escape it as `\%`: `0 2 * * * tar -czf /root/backups/crumbs-$(date +\%F).tgz -C /srv crumbs`. (Or put the command in a script and schedule the script.)

tasks.title: Retire Gary's job
tasks.text: Read `/usr/local/bin/cleanup-crumbs`. Every weekday night it deletes the whole crumbs folder, including the files your new backup job is about to save. Remove that job from the crontab, and **only** that job.

checks.fail_msg: cleanup-crumbs is still in root's crontab.

checks.cmd: crontab -l | grep -q bake-report && crontab -l | grep -q sync-sprinkles && crontab -l | grep -q /root/backups
checks.fail_msg: Your own jobs (bake-report, sync-sprinkles, the backup) should still be there.

hints: List the crontab, leave that one line out, and install the result. (With `crontab -e` on a real server you would delete the line, or put a `#` in front of it to keep it as a comment.)
In one line: `crontab -l | grep -v cleanup-crumbs | crontab -` (`grep -v` keeps every line that does **not** match). Careful: `crontab -r` would remove **all** jobs.
